messages:
sara: Hey team, apac model-serving started failing TLS handshakes right after yesterday's keystore RBAC change. KMS decrypts are returning AccessDenied.
mike: saw alerts. load balancer reported 502 then TLS handshake errors. any logs from the service?
ryan: snippet from model-serve pod logs:
```
2026-03-20T09:12:03Z ERROR tls: handshake error: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
2026-03-20T09:12:03Z WARN kms: decrypt failed: AccessDenied: user: arn:aws:iam::111111:role/keystore-operator is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt
```
lucy: that role change was part of the RBAC cleanup PR #4128 (revoke broad decrypt). I asked to gate rollout but it went through canary somehow.
sara: deploy-bot says canary rollout 2026-03-20T09:10. did the canary policy skip checks? @deploy-bot what happened?
deploy-bot: canary rollout 2026-03-20T09:10 initiated by ci/cd. No RBAC integration test failed. (automated)
mike: audit logs show keystore service principal had fewer kms:Decrypt events after 09:00; looking for missing entries in cloudtrail.
ryan: cloudtrail has some Deny entries but no x-request-id reference in app logs. I think audit-level ingestion for apac region is delayed.
sara: this is bad for us — TLS failures cause ML inference errors and downstream SLO breaches. Need rollback or emergency allow for keystore-operator in APAC KMS key policy.
lucy: proposal: rollback RBAC change for keystore-operator in apac namespaces, then rotate a short-lived key access role for staging, and add a targeted audit rule to log kms:Decrypt attempts with requestContext.sourceIp.
mike: add temporary policy:
```
{
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::111111:role/keystore-operator"},
  "Action": "kms:Decrypt",
  "Resource": "arn:aws:kms:ap-southeast-1:111111:key/abcd-1234"
}
```
ryan: we should avoid long-lived policy changes. I'll patch and restrict to the keystore podset annotation and add a TTL label.
sara: also noticed audit logs omit egress entries for several pods. we need to triage whether egress logging was dropped by the sidecar policy change earlier today.
lucy: cross-checking: sidecar config PR #4132 removed netpolicy egress capture. I'll re-enable minimal egress capture for keystore/ingest for 24h.
sec-bot: Security alert created: SE-2026-187 - Apac KMS decrypt denies leading to TLS handshake failures. Assigned to sec-eng oncall.
mike: vuln triage note: openssl CVE-2026-1111 was mentioned in an unrelated thread — not directly related but we should ensure our TLS configs aren't falling back to vulnerable ciphers. running quick scan.
ryan: quick mitigation plan:
- revert RBAC change in apac keystore (rollback PR)
- apply temporary KMS allow for keystore-operator with TTL
- re-enable egress audit capture for keystore pods
- rolling restart model-serving nodes in apac once decrypts succeed
- run TLS handshake smoke tests and update dashboard
sara: can someone take rollback now? I can own the rolling restart after rollback completes.
lucy: I'll open the rollback PR and patch egress capture. expecting <15m to get patch through canary gate and verify.
mike: I pushed a minimal KMS policy change to staging account. will request emergency approval for prod apac_key. pinging infra-sig.
sec-bot: Incident timeline updated. Please paste final remediation commands here when done.
sara: thanks. once done, we need to add automated guardrail: a CI check that runs a KMS decrypt with the post-change role in a dry-run before rollout, and an audit test ensuring cloudtrail decrypt entries show up within 2m.
ryan: noted. I'll create a ticket for the CI guardrail and the postmortem. tagging for follow-up: @mike @lucy @sara @sec-bot :thumbsup:
